_source: THE source of truth for effect content. data/effects.json is generated from this file by tools/pool-to-tables.mjs and must not be hand-edited.
_tags: `slots` are anatomy/location pairs; `*/<location>` means every anatomy that has that location. Only bludgeoning, piercing and slashing roll a hit location: every other damage type keeps ONE table per anatomy, tagged `<anatomy>/general` (or `*/general`), so an effect meant for fire or acid needs a general slot or its damage tags select nothing. `damageTypes` may be ["*"] for all eleven. `rank` is 1-12 and the severity band derives from it (1-3 minor, 4-6 moderate, 7-9 severe, 10-12 grave), as does the order of the three rows inside a band. `rank: null` means untriaged — see content/COVERAGE.md.
_pins: Optional `pins`: { "<damageType>/<anatomy>/<location>": <row> } forces this effect onto a specific row of a specific table, overriding the rank-driven placement.
_content: An entry is COMPLETE with `id` and `name`. Everything below is optional and additive, and no part of the engine assumes any of it exists. There is no `journal` — as of v2 the prose is ours and lives in `text`.
_text: `text` is the entry's prose, stored as HTML and enriched when the card renders. PF1's enrichers work in it, which is where `@Bleed[2d6;deep=20]`, `@Condition[stunned]` and `@Damage[1d6]` become clickable buttons. Use it for what the wound IS; use `note` for the one terse line the GM adjudicates from.
_conditions:
`conditions` is an array of PF1 conditions the effect imposes, by registry id (`dazed`, `stunned`, `deaf`, `prone`, `bleed`, …). Each is `{ id, duration?, bleed? }`.

`duration` absent means the condition stays until something takes it off. Present, it is `{ value, units, end? }` — `value` is a number or a dice formula rolled when the condition lands ("1d4"), `units` is turn/round/minute/hour/day, and `end` is turnStart (PF1's default), turnEnd or initiative. This is native PF1: the duration is written onto the condition's Active Effect, PF1 expires it against world time and DELETES it, and a GM can right-click the condition on the sheet to read or change the rounds left. "Until the end of your next turn" is { value: 1, units: "turn", end: "turnEnd" }.

`bleed` is valid only on the `bleed` condition and configures pf1-bleed-effects: `{ formula, ability?, mode?, deep? }`. `formula` is per-round damage; `ability` (str/dex/con/int/wis/cha) makes it ability bleed instead of hit points, with `mode` damage or drain; `deep` is hit points of dedicated healing needed to close the wound (Astora Homebrew rules, both modules). OMIT the whole block for an inert bleed marker — the vanilla PF1 condition, which is also what you get when pf1-bleed-effects isn't installed.
